claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar colony microstructure.
The starting alloy is brittle at room temperature.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal phase boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and premature or catastrophic failure.
A dilute Nb microalloying addition is the proposed single intervention.
Nb segregates to the internal lamellar phase boundaries.
Nb addition triggers in situ formation of nanoscale coherent Nb-rich precipitates at lamellar interfaces.
The coherent Nb-rich precipitates act as dislocation sinks that absorb and diffuse dislocations.
Interfacial precipitates reduce dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations.
The proposed precipitate-mediated dislocation behavior promotes more uniform plastic deformation and delays microcrack nucleation.
The intervention will increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the untreated alloy.
The intervention will significantly enhance room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The precipitates will not compromise the intrinsic strength of the alloy.
The proposed effect is applicable during room-temperature tensile loading.
The proposed effect applies at strain rates typical of structural applications.
The benefit will diminish if Nb segregation does not occur or precipitate coherence is lost under different thermal or strain-rate conditions.
The magnitude of the property improvements depends on Nb segregation and precipitation kinetics, which vary with processing parameters.
Failure to observe coherent interfacial Nb-rich precipitates or statistically significant simultaneous strength and ductility improvement would falsify the hypothesis.
